verdicts.rationale:
Step 1 (Clean Reproduction): Tested POST /collections/{c}/points/count with logically impossible range filter {"gte": 100, "lt": 50}. Server returns HTTP 200 with count=0, accepting invalid input without 4xx error. Tested with extreme boundary values (1.7976931348623157e+308, -1.7976931348623157e+308) - also accepted with HTTP 200. API contract violation confirmed.

Step 2 (Premise Audit): Developer cognition confirms 'Parameter validation on filter/condition APIs (min_should, value_count)' as a known blindspot. Bug shape 'qdrant-parameter-validation-numeric-boundary' explicitly targets missing Numeric Boundary validation. Premise holds.

Step 3 (Contract Verification): Contract specifies POST /collections/{c}/points/count accepts filter with Range condition having lt/gt/gte/lte fields. Contract states API should validate input but Range struct lacks validation constraints.

Step 4 (Source Grounding): Range<T> struct (lib/segment/src/types.rs:2787-2796) has NO #[validate(...)] attributes. No logical consistency checks (e.g., gte <= lt, gt < lte). check_range() function (lines 2812-2819) validates if a NUMBER fits in range, NOT if range parameters are valid. CountRequestInternal (lib/shard/src/count.rs:11-19) has #[validate(nested)] on filter, but Filter validation only recurses into Conditions, not Range boundaries. No boundary validation exists.

Step 5 (Falsification): Cannot falsify - reproduced successfully with impossible range (gte > lt). Server should return 400 Bad Request but returns 200 OK.

Step 6 (Triviality Exclusion): Not trivial. This is Type1_IllegalSuccess - API accepts semantically invalid input that violates mathematical logic (gte > lt is impossible for any number). Developer cognition confirms this is a recurring pattern (param_validation, 51 occurrences). 

Three-View Consensus: Contract perspective expects validation; source perspective shows no validation; reproduction perspective confirms acceptance of invalid input. CONFIRMED.
